title: Broken iPhone LCD buyback → China remanufacture → parts wholesale
one_liner: Pay repair shops for cracked screens, test LCDs, ship remanufacture-grade units, then sell remanufactured screens/parts back into the repair channel.
evidence_quote: hey, I want to buy your broken iPhone screens… we can recycle them in China… sell them as remanufactured units… scraped every single iPhone repair shop in the United States… $3 a unit for your broken iPhone screens and we'll send a prepaid shipping label
why_it_works: Turns shop waste into inbound trust, then upsells replacement parts; testing creates buy/sell spread. Mechanism from Chris Koerner's LCDcycle story — not a result promise.
notes: Same founding story in newsletter.chrisjkoerner.com/p/newsletter-0001 and YT chapter 'The Success of LCD Cycle' on https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gw0xjs1v_w0. No income guarantees.

title: Cult travel-stop brand snacks/merch ecommerce (Buc-ee's → Texas Snax pattern)
one_liner: Wholesale-buy iconic regional travel-stop snacks and merch, then sell online to fans who cannot visit the stores.
evidence_quote: You can check out our Buc-ee's snacks business here: https://texassnax.com … how something most people completely overlook turned into a real online business through Texas Snacks
why_it_works: Monetizes geographic scarcity around a cult offline brand that under-serves ecommerce. IP/reseller compliance is a hard gate.
notes: Related launch story: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l1RVNhFu058. Distinct from snack wholesale route sales (025).

title: Land bank near announced Buc-ee's / mega travel-stop sites
one_liner: Option or buy parcels beside newly announced mega travel centers before restaurants/hotels reprice the corridor.
evidence_quote: Entire economies spring up around new Buc-ee's locations — restaurants, hotels, retail — which can sharply reprice nearby land.
why_it_works: Public site announcements create a timing window before adjacency is fully priced. Capital- and legal-heavy; speculative.
notes: Supporting catalog page ideakoerner.com/idea/1430 cites this YT. Not investment advice.

title: Restaurant / QSR next to new Buc-ee's foot-traffic nodes
one_liner: Open or partner into food concepts beside new mega travel stops that pull dozens of pumps plus EV dwell traffic.
evidence_quote: Open a restaurant or food business near a new Buc-ee's location to ride the foot traffic from 50–150 pumps and Tesla Superchargers; multiple restaurants typically appear around each new site.
why_it_works: External traffic magnet subsidizes CAC versus building a destination from zero. Ops-heavy.
notes: Catalog mirror: ideakoerner.com/idea/1431.

title: Playmakers-style AI implementation agency for SMBs ($500–$5k/mo framing)
one_liner: Productized AI automation offer for local SMBs: voice agents, proposals, ops automations, sold as monthly retainers.
evidence_quote: Join Phil + learning 237 other AI beginners learning how to charge $500–$5k/mo: playmakersai.com … step-by-step business plan on how to AI automation agency from zero
why_it_works: Packages delivery templates + outbound for non-AI buyers; positioning is implementation retainers not chatbots-for-fun.
notes: Also CTA'd on https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=50iWtrj9Mkw. Fee ranges are framing, not guarantees.

title: Niche Zillow for RV parks / mobile-home parks / self-storage
one_liner: Unbundle CRE listings into a clean Zillow-like UX for one asset class (RV parks, MHPs, or self-storage) fed by public/scraped listing sources.
evidence_quote: Here's an idea I really love. The niche Zillow… RV parks, mobile home parks, self-storage… scrape and tap into other categories on Zillow and Crexi. Unbundle them
why_it_works: Vertical CRE UXes are weak; focused design + inventory aggregation can win attention before full two-sided liquidity. ToS/legal risk.
notes: From API-unbundling / tiny-tools episode. Counsel on scraping/ToS before build.

title: Apify/Clay/Zapier API-wrapper micro-SaaS (great unbundling)
one_liner: Wrap popular scrapers/enrichment APIs in a simpler vertical UI and sell recurring access to non-technical operators.
evidence_quote: API arbitrage and the great unbundling… same thing is happening today with tools like Apify, Clay, Zapier, OpenAI, and Claude… Nico… $3,500/month in recurring revenue with almost no technical background
why_it_works: Sells opinionated UX/workflow on top of commodity APIs; niche packaging is the product.
notes: Anecdotal MRR is illustrative only.

title: Portable self-storage containers on leased/owned land
one_liner: Place portable storage units on underused land and rent monthly pads/units without building traditional mini-storage.
evidence_quote: Portable self storage
why_it_works: Splits land control from storage demand; lower CapEx than stick-built facilities. Zoning/lease gates.
notes: Chapter on '40 Ways… Unwanted Land' episode; catalog detail at ideakoerner.com/idea/398.

title: Temporary/modular storage facilities on acreage
one_liner: Stand up temporary or modular storage on large parcels (owned or leased) as a land-monetization line.
evidence_quote: building temporary storage facilities… how you can use a lot of these ideas without ever owning a ranch yourself
why_it_works: Uses land optionality; temporary structures can move if highest-best-use changes.
notes: From Triple Eight Ranch solo episode on businesses found on the ranch.

title: RV park acquisition with hybrid nightly + monthly ops
one_liner: Acquire destination or workforce-adjacent RV parks and run mixed ADR: nightly tourists plus monthly long-stay pads.
evidence_quote: Buy existing RV parks in the $2-10 million range near destinations like state/national parks, lakes, or universities. Operate them with a hybrid model of short-term nightly stays ($60-90/night) and long-term monthly tenants ($600-1100/month)
why_it_works: Two demand curves stabilize occupancy; professional ops can reprice under-market pads. Capital gated.
notes: Also discussed with Jack Bosch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9w6UYrWzbCI. Figures illustrative, not forecasts.

title: Premium workforce RV park (anti-man-camp positioning)
one_liner: Buy/upgrade an RV park near oil/construction labor demand; differentiate with pad spacing, playgrounds/pools, cleaner ops vs low-quality man camps.
evidence_quote: Build or acquire an RV park in areas with high concentrations of blue-collar workers (oil workers, construction crews) and differentiate from existing low-quality 'man camps' by offering more space between pads, amenities like playgrounds and pools… validate demand by running competing Facebook Marketplace listings before committing capital.
why_it_works: Same labor demand, better product; Marketplace ads can falsify demand before CapEx.
notes: Workforce positioning detailed on ideakoerner.com/idea/685; paired with Koerner RV-park investment webinar cite.

title: Regional RV park roll-up under one consumer brand
one_liner: Consolidate fragmented mom-and-pop RV parks under a KOA-like brand to share ops/marketing and pursue a professionalized exit.
evidence_quote: Consolidate multiple small RV parks across a region under a single consumer-facing brand (like KOA) to achieve economies of scale, compress cap rates, and eventually exit to private equity. The sector is largely unconsolidated with most parks still mom-and-pop owned.
why_it_works: Fragmentation + weak branding can create platform value if shared systems work. Highly capital intensive.
notes: Roll-up framing on ideakoerner.com/idea/200. Not investment advice.

title: Attic insulation removal + high-R reinstall (subcontracted)
one_liner: FB-ads free attic inspection → remove old cellulose, air-seal, blow high-R fiberglass; subcontract labor, keep sales/ops.
evidence_quote: You Can Start This $1M/Yr Business With No Tools and No Crew … #InsulationBusiness #DuctCleaning #DuctSealing #HVACBusiness
why_it_works: High ticket + visual proof + subcontractability; marketing owns the wedge. Title anecdote ≠ guarantee.
notes: Detail: ideakoerner.com/idea/26.

title: Aeroseal / pressurized duct-sealing specialty
one_liner: Sell standalone or bundled duct sealing using pressurized sealant particle systems; attach to insulation/HVAC funnels.
evidence_quote: Seal leaky ductwork using Aeroseal technology, which pressurizes the duct system and sends sealant particles to automatically seal holes and cracks. Can be sold standalone or bundled with insulation services.
why_it_works: Narrow specialty with clear ROI story; bundles lift ticket size beside insulation.
notes: ideakoerner.com/idea/27. Brand certification/equipment may be required.

title: Home performance suite (insulation + ducts + air + HVAC upsells)
one_liner: One-metro home performance brand: free attic inspection ads → insulation, duct seal/clean, air scrubbers, HVAC referrals via subs.
evidence_quote: Comprehensive home energy and air quality business combining insulation, duct sealing, duct cleaning, air scrubbers, and HVAC upsells. Uses a subcontractor model requiring no tools or crew of your own, with Facebook ads driving free attic inspection leads.
why_it_works: Stacks attach rates on one lead; marketing + QC is the company. Distinct from single-SKU insulation.
notes: ideakoerner.com/idea/30.

title: Home toxin / indoor air-quality diagnostic assessments
one_liner: Charge for IAQ/toxin assessments with a remediation punch-list; monetize referrals to insulation/duct/HVAC partners.
evidence_quote: Diagnose homes for air quality issues and toxins, charging a few hundred dollars for an assessment and providing a detailed list of remediation recommendations. Can refer business to insulation, duct, and HVAC companies for commissions.
why_it_works: Low CapEx front door into higher-ticket remediation network. Claims/compliance care required.
notes: ideakoerner.com/idea/31.

title: Residential/commercial ductwork replacement & returns
one_liner: High-ticket duct replacement / add-returns / new-build duct installs as progression from cleaning/sealing niches.
evidence_quote: Replace and install new ductwork for residential and commercial properties, including new builds, adding returns, and full system replacements. Tickets range from $10,000-$15,000+. A natural progression from starting with duct cleaning
why_it_works: Messy specialty with fewer willing competitors; tickets support sales overhead. License/code gated.
notes: ideakoerner.com/idea/32.

title: AI digital + sales-ops partner for one high-ticket local service
one_liner: You own Maps/SEO/ads/AI systems; partner with a closer/operator on a $1k+ ticket home-service or B2B niche scored by the 100-pt rubric.
evidence_quote: ask your agent for a list of 30 high ticket local service offers… use my 100 pt opportunity score… Find an operating partner who excels at sales if that's not you. You focus on building the digital presence and making sure the phone rings.
why_it_works: Splits digital arbitrage from field sales — operator wedge, not just a research desk.
notes: Extension of opportunity-score desk (025) into partnership/ops form.

title: Zapier browser-skill client ops desk for boring businesses
one_liner: Productize Zapier's browser agent skill to automate repetitive back-office flows for Main Street clients (or run it in-house).
evidence_quote: automate these with @zapier … use this skill to do it fast (for yourself or clients!) https://github.com/boringmarketer/zapier-browser
why_it_works: Ships concrete automations instead of vague AI strategy; GitHub skill is the delivery artifact.
notes: Pairs with BM 'be boring / stop selling AI to AI people' positioning.

title: No-website / dead-review niche city takeover
one_liner: Pick a high-ticket boring niche where most operators lack sites/review replies; stand up digital presence + AI ops and take share city-by-city.
evidence_quote: 3/4 of the businesses in the niche didn't even have a website and the providers aren't even replying to google reviews … $1,000+ average ticket size … you just need to be 10%+ better than the competitors in digital presence, marketing, ops, customer service: THIS IS WHERE YOU USE AI
why_it_works: Competition is offline-weak; a small digital edge compounds in one metro niche.
notes: City-level boring-niche receipts thread.
